podcast.body: Released as Def Jam's second single in 1985, this track was soon withdrawn due to containing illegal samples from AC/DC's song "Back in Black." The Beastie Boys had neglected to ask permission, and AC/DC was categorically against sampling at the time. It became a significant collectible for years until it was reissued in Europe in 2007 with AC/DC's blessing, after the Beasties had become hugely successful and could speak directly with AC/DC's peers, who had softened their stance. "The label's second single was a Beastie's track called Rock Hard, but it was soon withdrawn because it contained some illegal AC-DC samples from the song Back in Black."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track, released in 1985, was the second single from Def Jam but was quickly withdrawn due to containing unauthorized samples from ACDC's "Back in Black." ACDC was famously against sampling and had not given permission. The single became a collector's item but was eventually reissued in Europe in 2007 with ACDC's blessing, as the Beastie Boys had become successful enough to negotiate directly with ACDC's members. "The Beastie boys with Rock Hard, with the original illegal ACDC samples intact."
